proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 4 (Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 '⇒' via the proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' and Remark 1.8(1)); the argument there uses the compact multiplicity pieces only through C ⊆ M ∩ N_i, so it applies verbatim to one Lipschitz piece N = F(C) without disjointifying. No errata apply.

Conventions. n ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 0; E := Ambient n ℓ; ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ := volume; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (= Lⁿ on ℝⁿ); B_ρ(z) := closedBall z ρ; ‖f‖ := sup|f|. a = (M, θ) is an admissible pair (IsRectifiablePair): M is countably n-rectifiable and Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K. μ := (mk a).weight. (C, F) satisfies (P1) C ⊆ ℝⁿ compact; (P2) F is κ-Lipschitz (κ ≥ 0); (P3) F is differentiable at each w ∈ C with injective DF(w) := fderiv ℝ F w; (P4) DF is continuous on C; (P5) c|v − w| ≤ |F(v) − F(w)| on C with c > 0. N := F(C). "The claim at x" means: for every w ∈ C with F(w) = x and every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) → θ(x)·∫_{range DF(w)} f dHⁿ as t ↓ 0 (t > 0). We must show that the claim holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x.
Results used (pinned; standard axioms only):
- Sibling ts_piece_density_blowup (applied to n, ℓ, C, F, using 0 < n and the piece hypotheses): (3b) there is Γ ∈ ℝ with Hⁿ(N ∩ B_ρ(z)) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all z ∈ N and ρ > 0; (3a) for every w ∈ C with Lⁿ(C ∩ B_r(w))/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) → 1 (r ↓ 0) and every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ): (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_N f(t⁻¹(y − F(w))) dHⁿ(y) → ∫_{range DF(w)} f dHⁿ.
- (R2b) SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn: Hⁿ(F(S)) ≤ κⁿ·Lⁿ(S) for S ⊆ ℝⁿ.
- Lebesgue density theorem, Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div (μ := volume on ℝⁿ, s := C).
- Lusin's theorem, SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable, for a measure that is closed-inner-regular on finite-measure measurable sets; a finite Borel measure on E is weakly regular, so this holds by Mathlib MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt.
- Upper density theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6), SimonGMT Chapter01.ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside together with Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular and Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure: if ν is a Borel measure on E and A ⊆ E is Borel with ν(A) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A, ν(A ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0. (In the library the conclusion is "dimensionalUpperDensity ν.toOuterMeasure n A x = 0", the limsup as r ↓ 0 of ν(A ∩ B_r(x))/(realUnitBallVolume n·ofReal(r)ⁿ) with the constant realUnitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞); a vanishing limsup of nonnegative quantities is a limit 0; Borel sets are Carathéodory measurable for ν.toOuterMeasure; the a.e. is for simonHausdorffMeasureReal n = μHE[n].)

Proof.

1. The weight. By definition (mk a).weight = pairWeight n M θ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(z ↦ ofReal θ(z)) (Quot.lift evaluated on the class of a; definitional).
(a) θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M: M = ⋃_{k∈ℕ} (M ∩ B_k(0)) and θ is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, on each M ∩ B_k(0) (B_k(0) is compact); use Mathlib aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff.
(b) For Borel S ⊆ E: μ(S) = ∫⁻_{M∩S} ofReal θ dHⁿ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict); in particular μ(K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K}|θ| dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K.
(c) For Borel S and a bounded Borel g: E → ℝ vanishing outside a bounded set, g is μ-integrable and ∫_S g dμ = ∫_{M∩S} g·θ dHⁿ: by Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ (density ofReal∘θ is a.e.-measurable by (a) and finite), ∫ g dμ = ∫ (ofReal θ(z)).toReal·g(z) d(Hⁿ⌞M)(z) and (ofReal θ(z)).toReal = θ(z) for z ∈ M, which holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (ae_restrict_mem₀, M null-measurable); integrability follows from (b) and boundedness.

2. Piece facts. F is injective on C by (P5); for z ∈ N let ψ(z) be the unique w ∈ C with F(w) = z. N is compact, hence Borel, and Hⁿ(N) ≤ κⁿ·Lⁿ(C) < ∞ by (R2b). Fix Γ as in (3b) and put Γ⁺ := max(Γ, 0) ≥ 0; then Hⁿ(N ∩ B_ρ(z)) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) ≤ ofReal(Γ⁺ρⁿ), so (tⁿ)⁻¹·Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{Rt}(z)).toReal ≤ Γ⁺Rⁿ for all z ∈ N and R, t > 0 (the measure is finite).

3. Density points. By the Lebesgue density theorem, Lⁿ(C ∩ B_r(w))/Lⁿ(B_r(w)) → 1 (r ↓ 0) for Lⁿ⌞C-a.e. w. Let Z be the set of w ∈ C at which this fails. Since C is Borel, Lⁿ(Z) = Lⁿ(Z ∩ C) = (Lⁿ⌞C)(Z) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply'). By (R2b), Hⁿ(F(Z)) ≤ κⁿ·Lⁿ(Z) = 0. If x ∈ N ∖ F(Z), then ψ(x) ∉ Z, i.e. ψ(x) is a density point of C.

4. Reduction. Since M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x lies in M (Mathlib ae_restrict_mem₀), so points outside M may be ignored. If x ∉ N, no w ∈ C satisfies F(w) = x, so the claim at x holds vacuously. Every Hⁿ-null set is Hⁿ⌞M-null. Hence it suffices to construct countably many compact sets C_k ⊆ M ∩ N such that (i) Hⁿ((M ∩ N) ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0, (ii) θ restricted to each C_k is continuous, and (iii) for each k the claim holds at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C_k. Then the claim fails only on (E ∖ M) ∪ ((M ∩ N) ∖ ⋃_k C_k) ∪ ⋃_k (exceptional set in C_k): the first set is Hⁿ⌞M-null and the others are Hⁿ-null.

5. Construction of the C_k (Lusin pieces). By 1(a) choose a Borel function θ̃: E → ℝ with θ = θ̃ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (AEMeasurable.mk). Choose a Borel set S ⊇ {z : θ(z) ≠ θ̃(z)} with (Hⁿ⌞M)(S) = 0 (measurable null hull), and a Borel set M' ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ M') = 0 (M is Hⁿ-null-measurable). Then Hⁿ(M' ∩ S) = (Hⁿ⌞M)(M' ∩ S) ≤ (Hⁿ⌞M)(S) = 0 (M' ∩ S ⊆ M is Borel). For integers q ≥ 1 put
A_q := (M' ∖ S) ∩ N ∩ {θ̃ ≥ 1/q} ∩ B_q(0),
a Borel set. On A_q ⊆ M ∖ S we have θ = θ̃ ≥ 1/q, so Hⁿ(A_q) ≤ q·∫_{M∩B_q(0)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (Chebyshev). For integers m ≥ 1 apply Lusin's theorem to the finite Borel measure ν_q := Hⁿ⌞A_q, the Borel set A_q (ν_q(A_q) < ∞) and the Borel function θ̃: there is a closed set C_{q,m} ⊆ A_q with Hⁿ(A_q ∖ C_{q,m}) = ν_q(A_q ∖ C_{q,m}) < 1/m on which θ̃ is continuous. C_{q,m} is closed and bounded (⊆ B_q(0)), hence compact; C_{q,m} ⊆ A_q ⊆ M ∩ N; and θ = θ̃ on C_{q,m} (⊆ M' ∖ S), so θ restricted to C_{q,m} is continuous. Covering: if x ∈ (M ∩ N) ∖ ((M ∖ M') ∪ (M' ∩ S)), then x ∈ (M' ∖ S) ∩ N and θ̃(x) = θ(x) > 0, so x ∈ A_q for every integer q ≥ max(1/θ(x), |x|). Therefore
(M ∩ N) ∖ ⋃_{q,m} C_{q,m} ⊆ (M ∖ M') ∪ (M' ∩ S) ∪ ⋃_q (A_q ∖ ⋃_m C_{q,m}),
and Hⁿ(A_q ∖ ⋃_m C_{q,m}) ≤ inf_m 1/m = 0. So the countable family (C_{q,m}) satisfies (i) and (ii).

6. Two upper-density estimates. Fix one of these compact sets C' := C_{q,m} and r_0 > 0 with C' ⊆ ball(0, r_0). Apply the upper density theorem twice:
(a) ν := μ (a Borel measure) and A_a := B_{r_0}(0) ∖ C' (Borel; μ(A_a) ≤ μ(B_{r_0}(0)) < ∞ by 1(b));
(b) ν := Hⁿ⌞N and A_b := N ∖ C' (Borel; ν(A_b) ≤ Hⁿ(N) < ∞).
Points of C' lie outside A_a and A_b. Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C': μ(A_a ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 and Hⁿ(A_b ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0. For such x and every R > 0, as t ↓ 0:
(a') (tⁿ)⁻¹·μ(B_{Rt}(x) ∖ C') → 0: when 0 < Rt < r_0 − |x| we have B_{Rt}(x) ⊆ ball(0, r_0), so B_{Rt}(x) ∖ C' = A_a ∩ B_{Rt}(x), and (tⁿ)⁻¹μ(A_a ∩ B_{Rt}(x)) = Rⁿ·μ(A_a ∩ B_{Rt}(x))/(Rt)ⁿ;
(b') (tⁿ)⁻¹·Hⁿ((N ∖ C') ∩ B_{Rt}(x)) = Rⁿ·Hⁿ(A_b ∩ B_{Rt}(x))/(Rt)ⁿ → 0.

7. The blow-up at a good point. Let x ∈ C' be a point satisfying (a') and (b') for every R > 0 and x ∉ F(Z); by steps 3 and 6 this holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C'. Let w ∈ C with F(w) = x; then w = ψ(x) (step 2) and w is a density point of C (step 3). Put T := range DF(w). Fix f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) and R > 0 with f(z) = 0 for |z| > R; for t > 0 let g_t(y) := f(t⁻¹(y − x)), a continuous function with |g_t| ≤ ‖f‖ that vanishes outside B_{Rt}(x). By 1(c) and C' ⊆ M ∩ N (C', N Borel),
(tⁿ)⁻¹∫ g_t dμ = (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_M g_t·θ dHⁿ = I_1 + I_2 + I_3 + I_4,
I_1 := θ(x)·(tⁿ)⁻¹∫_N g_t dHⁿ,
I_2 := −θ(x)·(tⁿ)⁻¹∫_{N∖C'} g_t dHⁿ,
I_3 := (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_{C'} g_t(y)·(θ(y) − θ(x)) dHⁿ(y),
I_4 := (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_{M∖C'} g_t·θ dHⁿ = (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_{E∖C'} g_t dμ.
[Indeed I_1 + I_2 = θ(x)(tⁿ)⁻¹∫_{C'} g_t dHⁿ; adding I_3 gives (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_{C'} g_tθ dHⁿ; adding I_4 gives (tⁿ)⁻¹∫_M g_tθ dHⁿ. All integrals are finite: Hⁿ(N) < ∞; θ is continuous, hence bounded, on the compact C'; g_tθ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable since g_t is bounded and vanishes outside the compact B_{Rt}(x) on which θ is integrable over M; the last equality is 1(c) with S = E ∖ C'.]
(i) I_1 → θ(x)·∫_T f dHⁿ by (3a) of the sibling, since w is a density point of C and F(w) = x.
(ii) |I_2| ≤ θ(x)·‖f‖·(tⁿ)⁻¹·Hⁿ((N ∖ C') ∩ B_{Rt}(x)) → 0 by (b').
(iii) |I_3| ≤ ‖f‖·sup{|θ(y) − θ(x)| : y ∈ C' ∩ B_{Rt}(x)}·(tⁿ)⁻¹·Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{Rt}(x)) ≤ ‖f‖·Γ⁺·Rⁿ·sup{|θ(y) − θ(x)| : y ∈ C' ∩ B_{Rt}(x)} → 0, by (3b) at x ∈ N (in the form of step 2 with Γ⁺) and the continuity of θ restricted to C' at x.
(iv) |I_4| ≤ ‖f‖·(tⁿ)⁻¹·μ(B_{Rt}(x) ∖ C') → 0 by (a').
Hence (tⁿ)⁻¹∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) → θ(x)·∫_{range DF(w)} f dHⁿ. Since f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) and the (unique) w were arbitrary, the claim holds at x.

8. Conclusion. By step 7, for each C_{q,m} the claim holds at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C_{q,m}; by step 5 these countably many compact sets cover M ∩ N up to an Hⁿ-null set; points of E ∖ M form an Hⁿ⌞M-null set and points of M ∖ N satisfy the claim vacuously; by step 4 the claim therefore holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, which is the theorem. ∎
